caveat: Backtested on the synthetic six-month history, whose price process the generator defined — inflation, FX pass-through, a regional premium and decaying shocks. A model evaluated on data generated by known rules will do better than one facing real markets, so read these as an upper bound. The interval-coverage figure is the more transferable of the two: a model that cannot calibrate its own uncertainty on easy data will not manage it on hard data.
